page: Vultr vbm-4c-32gb is a dedicated bare metal server belonging to the Bare Metal SSD family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 1270 processor built on the x86_64 architecture, providing 4 physical cores and 8 vCPUs via hyperthreading. The CPU operates at a dedicated clock speed of 3.8 GHz and is supported by an 8 MB L3 cache. The hardware configuration is completed by 32.0 GB of system memory, 480 GB of local SSD storage, and one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across most compute workloads. The single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests fall into the middle 50% tier, with scores of 1728.79 and 8815.11 respectively. Passmark CPU testing yields an average score of 9737.8. While cached small-block memory read bandwidth is average at 494.72 GB/sec, large-block uncached memory read and write speeds are weak, measuring 31.11 GB/sec and 14.73 GB/sec. Conversely, the Passmark memory score is top-tier, ranking in the top 10% of tested systems.

This server is qualitatively cost-efficient for users requiring dedicated, non-virtualized hardware without the overhead of a hypervisor. It is well-suited for general-purpose workloads, static web serving, and database operations, as demonstrated by an average of 8.08 million Redis SET operations per second. However, it is poorly suited for larger machine learning tasks, with medium 7B LLM prompt processing dropping to a poor 16.42 tokens/sec.
